title: Your life is not your own
author: Wisani Hlungwana
body:
Your life is not your own\

Many of us think that God called us to live our lives to the fullest and for our own enjoyment. The sooner we realise that our lives are essentially vessels that God uses for his will and purposes, the easier it will be to surrender our lives to him. The highest form of submission is surrendering our will to God’s will.
We were never meant to be born again (saved) and be Christians and it ends there. We are born with a mandate, to which we will give account when we go back to the Father, our Lord God.\

Some are called to be intercessors, givers, evangelists and pastors, church elders and leaders, parents, counsellors and many other spiritual gifts *“There are different kinds of gifts, but the same Spirit distributes them. There are different kinds of service, but the same Lord. There are different kinds of working, but in all of them and in everyone it is the same God at work.” -* 1 Corinthians 12:4–6\

Let’s look at the life of Mary the mother of Jesus. A young woman betrothed to Joseph has her life suddenly ‘disrupted’ by God. She finds tremendous favour from God in that she’d be impregnated by the Holy Spirit and ultimately give birth to the Saviour of the whole world.
Upon receiving the prophecy and word from angel Gabriel, she utters these words in Luke 1:38, “I am the Lord’s servant. May everything you have said about me come true.” She gave her life away to be used by God as a midwife of the salvation of the entire world. What a privilege and honour it to be found worthy enough to be his ambassadors and embodiment of his will. \

Paul was first a persecutor of the Church but is later converted into an intense advocate of the church he used to attack. When he encounters God on his way to Damascus, the Lord speaks to Ananias the disciple to pray over Paul as God had ordained him. God utters these words to Ananias concerning Paul, “he is a chosen vessel of Mine to bear My name before Gentiles, kings, and the children of Israel.” — Acts 9:15. When we study the life of Paul, he embodied this calling throughout! 
If we desire to be used by God, we ought to understand that our life is never our own. We must be willing to lay it down at the altar as an ever-living sacrifice.
In closing, let’s have a look at Isaiah 9 where God pours out his desire and need for men and women to serve his purposes.
““I have been treading the winepress alone; no one was there to help me. In my anger I have trampled my enemies as if they were grapes. In my fury I have trampled my foes. Their blood has stained my clothes. For the time has come for me to avenge my people, to ransom them from their oppressors. I was amazed to see that no one intervened to help the oppressed. So I myself stepped in to save them with my strong arm, and my wrath sustained me. I crushed the nations in my anger and made them stagger and fall to the ground, spilling their blood upon the earth.”” – Isaiah‬ ‭63‬:‭3‬-‭6‬ ‭NLT‬‬\

Will you avail your life to God’s need? God is treading daily looking for those who administer to bring justice; take care of the orphans and widows; call many into salvation through evangelism; intercessors for the nations; righteous leaders in the market place; and marriages that demonstrate his love for the Church and so much more! Whether be it a role or calling, God wants you to partner with Him. \

Ask God today what His purpose and will is for your life. Ask Him to use you as his vessel. Be willing to surrender without negotiating and wanting Him to fulfil his will according to your terms and conditions. ⁠Servants do not debate with the Master; theirs is to simply obey and follow instructions from the Lord!
